title: Ship alert rules for auto-rollback triggers + stale/missing rollout SLO monitors (routing + paging policy)
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
We’re enabling auto-rollback/pause for rollouts based on SLO breach evaluation. We need production-quality alerting around (a) auto-actions firing, (b) suppression/override usage, and (c) missing/stale monitors that prevent evaluation.

This ticket is owned by Obs/SRE. It covers Grafana/Prometheus alert rules, Alertmanager routing, and Slack/oncall destinations. Goal is to ensure the *right* people get notified/paged with enough context to act, without generating paging storms during rollouts.

Primary audiences:
- SRE oncall (platform reliability)
- Service owner oncall (route/model owners) for high-severity rollouts
- Release eng + Console/Platform engineers during staged enablement
acceptance_criteria: Alert rules exist for auto-rollback/auto-pause events with clear severity levels and dedupe keys; rules fire in staging and can be validated via synthetic signals.
Alert rules exist for monitor missing/stale and evaluation suppressed; missing/stale should be actionable and not page by default unless auto-rollback is enabled for the rollout/service.

Alert routing sends:
- SEV1 pages to SRE oncall for production regressions where auto-rollback fails OR repeated auto-rollbacks suggest systemic issues.
- SEV2 Slack notifications to #eng-sre and #eng-platform (and optionally service owner channel where mapping exists).
- SEV3/INFO notifications for suppressed rollbacks and monitor staleness to #eng-sre (non-paging).

Each alert payload includes: rollout_id, service/route, model_version (candidate + baseline), region, customer_tier, decision (rollback/pause/suppress), suppression_reason (if any), monitor_id(s), and dashboard/runbook links.
Alerts are documented in the oncall runbook (ENG-4855) with triage steps and common false-positive scenarios (telemetry lag, low traffic).
Noise controls implemented: minimum firing duration, grouping, inhibit rules during known telemetry outages, and label/cardinality constraints are respected.
implementation_notes:
Proposed signals (metrics from redwood + slo-toolkit integration):
- rollouts_slo_eval_total{outcome=breach|ok|unknown, reason=...}
- rollouts_auto_action_total{action=rollback|pause|none, result=success|failed|suppressed, suppression_reason=...}
- rollouts_monitor_state{state=ok|stale|missing} (or derive from eval outcome=unknown + reason=monitor_missing|monitor_stale)

Alert rule sketches (PromQL names are representative; final names should follow observability standard):
1) Auto-rollback executed (notify, not page by default):
- Condition: increase(rollouts_auto_action_total{action="rollback", result="success"}[5m]) > 0
- Severity: warn
- Routing: #eng-sre + #eng-platform; include rollout_id and scope labels

2) Auto-rollback failed (page):
- Condition: increase(rollouts_auto_action_total{action="rollback", result="failed"}[10m]) > 0
- Severity: critical
- Routing: SRE oncall (PagerDuty) + #incidents (Slack)
- Notes: include error_code/error_class label if available; otherwise link to controller logs via trace/correlation id

3) Repeated auto-rollbacks for same service/route (page if >N in 60m):
- Condition: sum by (service, route, region) (increase(rollouts_auto_action_total{action="rollback", result="success"}[60m])) >= 3
- Severity: critical
- Rationale: indicates systemic perf regression or unsafe policy thresholds

4) Monitor missing/stale for auto-rollback-enabled rollout (notify; page only if rollout progressing):
- Condition: rollouts_monitor_state{state=~"missing|stale"} == 1 for 15m
- Add gating: rollout_auto_actions_enabled == 1 AND rollout_state=~"canary|ab_test|ramping"
- Severity: warn (page if ‘enabled + ramping’ and >30m)

5) Rollback suppressed (info):
- Condition: increase(rollouts_auto_action_total{result="suppressed"}[15m]) > 0
- Severity: info
- Routing: #eng-sre
- Purpose: audit/awareness; not actionable unless unexpected.

Routing / grouping guidance:
- Group by: alertname, service, route, region, rollout_id (rollout_id may be optional if too high-cardinality; if so, use rollout_hash and put rollout_id in annotation only).
- Inhibit: if TelemetryDown/PrometheusIngestLag global alert is firing, inhibit staleness/missing alerts.
- Slack notifications should be concise; link out to Grafana dashboard panel + runbook section.

Open question: whether we can route to service-owner oncall automatically. If we have a stable mapping (service -> PD service / Slack channel) in config, we can add a second receiver. If not, keep to SRE + eng-platform for MVP and rely on incident process to pull in owners.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12 (Aisha Bello): Drafted alert taxonomy + initial routing proposal (page only on rollback failure / repeated rollbacks; staleness notify). Waiting on final metric names from ENG-4837 to avoid rework.

2026-02-18 (Allison Grant): Reviewed for label/cardinality risks. Recommendation: keep rollout_id out of labels in alert rules; include it only in annotations from exemplars/log search where possible.

2026-02-20 (Sean Gallagher): Confirmed paging policy with oncall leads: rollback failure is page-worthy; successful rollback is Slack notify; staleness is notify unless rollout is actively ramping and auto-actions enabled.

2026-02-24 (Aisha Bello): Implemented rules + receivers in observability-pack (PR-913) and validated in staging using synthetic SLO breach + forced stale monitor. Added inhibit rule tied to TelemetryIngestLag to reduce noise during known outages.
review_notes: Need explicit runbook links in annotations (runbook section anchors) so incident-bot messages and alerts point to the same triage steps.
Ensure Alertmanager grouping doesn’t collapse multiple different rollouts into one thread; grouping should include service/route/region and (if safe) rollout_key derived from rollout_id.
Confirm that alerts are gated by rollout_auto_actions_enabled to avoid noise for services not opted into the feature.
next_steps: Land PR-913 to observability-pack after final review from Sean Gallagher + Allison Grant.
Coordinate with ENG-4872 (incident-bot) so Slack notifications for auto-rollback use the same dashboard/runbook links as alert rules (avoid two competing formats).
Add a short section to ENG-4855 runbook: alert definitions, severities, and when to page service owners.
Post-rollout: evaluate alert volume and tune thresholds (especially repeated rollback threshold) after first internal prod canary.
